positive_prompts.prompt: Audit the shielded pool logic of our mixer: deposits insert note commitments into an on-chain Merkle tree, withdrawals reveal a nullifier derived from the note secret, and the contract tracks a spent-nullifier mapping. I want the nullifier derivation, uniqueness, and spent-set semantics checked for double-spend and cross-pool replay.

Review our shielded transfer protocol's state transitions: join-split of input notes into output notes with value commitments, change outputs linked back to the sender, and withdrawal transactions that can be front-run by relayers. Check ownership binding of notes, replay domains across chain forks, and deposit/withdraw ordering assumptions.

negative_prompts.prompt: Audit this standalone incremental Merkle tree library: leaf insertion, inclusion proof verification, sparse tree defaults for empty subtrees, and second-preimage domain separation between leaves and internal nodes. It is a generic library with no shielded pool or nullifier logic on top.

Review this Circom withdrawal circuit only for constraint completeness: are all witness signals properly constrained, is the nullifier hash computed with correctly constrained components, and can a malicious prover satisfy the circuit with an unconstrained intermediate signal? The contract-side pool logic is out of scope.

output_fields_present: tree variant and proof path under review
